newsitem.title: UK: M.Grenfell Kepit bid knocked by suspensions - funds.
newsitem.headline: M.Grenfell Kepit bid knocked by suspensions - funds.

text.p: The revelation on Monday that Morgan Grenfell had suspended dealing in its high-profile European funds could affect its lobbying for the Kleinwort European Privatisation fund (KEPIT), industry sources said.

But a spokesman for Morgan Grenfell, which has some 70 billion stg under management, said the bid and the suspension were "completely unrelated" and linking them was "baloney". He added, "The investigation is still being conducted and we can't say more until it is complete."

The suspension comes two weeks after 10 separate companies approached the independent board of the 500 million sterling KEPIT fund to manage it. Morgan Grenfell, the fund management arm of investment bank Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, was among the contenders.

Morgan Grenfell suspended dealing in three funds -- its 788 million stg Dublin-listed MG European Growth Trust, the 134 million stg MG Europa and the 445 million stg MG European Capital Growth fund pending investigation into "possible irregularities centring on certain unquoted securities" held by the funds.

"IMRO is working closely with Morgan Grenfell to investigate whether there were any irregularities and to what extent the funds were affected," said Judy Delaforce at IMRO, the UK's Investment Management Regulatory Organisation.
It is not yet an official enquiry, she added.
Peter Young, who manages the Capital Growth and European Growth funds, has been suspended while the company examines the unquoted securities, Morgan Grenfell told Reuters.
The Europa fund also had some unlisted securities in it but its manager is not being questioned.

Morgan Grenfell was widely considered one of the frontrunners to manage the KEPIT fund, with an excellent track record and the formidable resources behind it to handle such a large fund. It was thought to want to broaden KEPIT's mandate to a general European fund. Under former fund manager John Armitage, its European Growth Fund was the seventh best performer among 119 similar funds over three years and second out of 112 over five years.

But recent performance has been less than sparkling, mainly, fund research sources said, because of one or two large technology bets in Europe that went badly. "Has it affected their KEPIT bid?" asked one fund manager. "Did last week's news from Fleming affect their bid? Of course it must. These are some of the biggest, highest-profile European funds held by all the main pension funds and institutions."

Last week, days after Fleming approached the KEPIT board to run the Kelinwort fund, the Robert Fleming Group was fined some 700,000 stg by IMRO after a fund manager was found pocketing trading profits.
The group stressed the breaches had "no bearing" on any portfolios managed by Robert Fleming companies elsewhere.
Morgan Grenfell said the performance of their Europe funds had little direct bearing on their KEPIT bid because Young would never have been in line to manage KEPIT if they secured the mandate.

Fund managers said there was intense interest in the suspension of the funds because several had noticed the market value of their unquoted holdings were unusually high. A maximum of 10 percent of the Morgan Grenfell funds may be held in "unapproved securities". "We had queried our own compliance officer about it but we were told we couldn't hold such weightings," said one.
